latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Total body burden of clonal CD20+ aggressive B-cell lymphoma (nodal + extranodal). Drives lymphadenopathy, mass effect, LDH release, and prognosis (IPI). Reuses concept of lymphoma_tumor_burden_activity but specific to aggressive DLBCL kinetics.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: High-grade proliferative kinetics (Ki-67 high, double/triple hit)
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Rapid mitotic turnover with very high proliferation index (Ki-67 often >80%, up to ~100% in HGBCL with MYC and BCL2/BCL6 rearrangement). Drives extreme LDH elevation, tumor lysis risk, rapid clinical progression, and CNS dissemination tendency.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Rapid lymphoma cell turnover and intracellular enzyme release
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Spontaneous and treatment-induced apoptosis of high-turnover lymphoma cells releases LDH, urate, K+, and PO4 into circulation. Underlies LDH as both diagnostic clue and IPI risk factor, and TLS pathophysiology.

IL-6/TNF/IFN-γ-driven constitutional inflammation from lymphoma microenvironment. Causes B-symptoms (fever >38°C, drenching night sweats, weight loss >10%/6mo), low albumin, low Hb, and elevated CRP/ferritin without infection.

Direct lymphomatous infiltration of bone marrow (10-20% of de novo DLBCL; concordant large-cell vs discordant low-grade infiltration). Causes peripheral cytopenias (anemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia) and is a stage-IV-defining feature.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Extranodal organ infiltration and mass effect
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Extranodal involvement (GI tract, testis, kidney/adrenal, breast, bone, skin, paraspinal) causes site-specific symptoms: GI bleeding/perforation, ureteric obstruction, adrenal insufficiency, cord compression. Independent IPI risk factor when ≥2 sites involved.

Leptomeningeal or parenchymal CNS infiltration. Occurs in ~5% at diagnosis or relapse; risk stratified by CNS-IPI (age, LDH, ECOG, stage, extranodal sites, kidney/adrenal involvement). Accounts for poor-prognosis CNS relapse despite systemic remission.

Loss of normal B-cell repertoire and hypogammaglobulinemia from displacement of normal lymphoid tissue and rituximab-induced B-cell depletion. Predisposes to encapsulated organism, viral, and PCP infections; exacerbated by chemotherapy.

EBV-positive DLBCL NOS (often elderly, immunosenescent or post-transplant). EBER-ISH positive; LMP1/EBNA2 expression drives NF-kB activation. Worse prognosis with R-CHOP. Distinct from EBV-negative majority.

Rapid release of intracellular K+, PO4, and nucleic acids (→ uric acid via xanthine oxidase) from dying lymphoma cells. Risk highest in bulky disease, high LDH, high WBC, high-grade variants, in first 1-7 days of cytotoxic therapy or steroid pre-phase.

Treatment-induced myelosuppression from cyclophosphamide/doxorubicin/etoposide. Nadir ANC at days 7-14 of each cycle; predisposes to febrile neutropenia and opportunistic infection. Distinct from infiltrative cytopenia (M_DLBCL_BONE_MARROW_INFILTRATION).

latent_mechanisms.display_name: CAR-T / bispecific cytokine release syndrome and ICANS pathophysiology
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Massive T-cell activation against CD19/CD20 on lymphoma → IL-6/IFN-γ/IL-1 surge (CRS) plus blood-brain-barrier disruption (ICANS). Onset typically days 1-7 post-CAR-T; days 1-3 with bispecifics. Drives fever, hypotension, hypoxia, encephalopathy.

Topoisomerase-IIβ-mediated cardiomyocyte injury, dose-dependent. Risk rises sharply >300 mg/m² doxorubicin (R-CHOP exposes ~300 mg/m² over 6 cycles). Causes LVEF decline, late-onset heart failure (months-years).

B-cell depletion abrogates anti-HBV humoral control; in HBsAg+ or HBsAg-/anti-HBc+ patients, viral replication resumes during/after therapy, with delayed hepatitis flare often after rituximab last dose. Can cause fulminant hepatitis if not prophylaxed.

Cumulative effect of B-cell depletion (rituximab), neutropenia, lymphopenia, steroid exposure, and CD19/CD20-targeted therapy on infection susceptibility. Predisposes to PCP, encapsulated bacteria, HBV/CMV/VZV reactivation, invasive fungal infection.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Primary splenic / isolated extranodal DLBCL distribution
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: An anatomic distribution of DLBCL in which disease is dominated by splenic parenchymal involvement and may lack clinically apparent lymphadenopathy. It explains abdominal pain, early satiety, splenomegaly, splenic nodules, high LDH, and the absence of nodal disease without excluding DLBCL.
An anatomic distribution of DLBCL in which disease is expressed as pathologic lymphadenopathy or nodal mass. This is common, but it is not required for extranodal or primary splenic DLBCL.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Splenic involvement present (~30-40% of stage III-IV DLBCL).
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Direct splenic infiltration by lymphoma; can be diffuse or nodular pattern on imaging.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Hepatic involvement.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Hepatic lymphomatous infiltration causes hepatomegaly with variable transaminase rise.
sIL-2R (sCD25) shed from activated lymphocytes correlates with tumor burden and is a Japanese-textbook prognostic marker for malignant lymphoma; commonly elevated >1000 U/mL in DLBCL.
β2-microglobulin shed from lymphoma cell surface MHC-I; correlates with tumor burden and renal function; included in some prognostic indices.
FDG-avid in essentially all DLBCL; SUVmax often 10-30 at diagnosis. PET-CT defines staging and is the response-assessment standard (Deauville 5-PS).
High Ki-67 and double/triple-hit kinetics drive accelerated apoptosis-proliferation cycle, releasing intracellular contents.
Highly proliferative tumors are most susceptible to spontaneous and treatment-induced TLS.
LDH elevation is a key IPI factor; reflects both tumor burden and proliferation rate. Often 1.5-5× ULN in advanced disease.
LDH/ULN ratio is the IPI-relevant scaled metric (cutoff >1).
Nucleic acid degradation → uric acid via xanthine oxidase; can crystallize in renal tubules causing AKI.
Intracellular K+ release → hyperkalemia, arrhythmia risk.
Intracellular phosphate release; complexes with calcium to cause secondary hypocalcemia.
Hyperphosphatemia drives calcium phosphate precipitation → hypocalcemia, tetany risk.
Urate and calcium-phosphate crystal nephropathy; AKI is a Cairo-Bishop clinical TLS criterion.
Defines clinical TLS with Cairo-Bishop criteria; major early-treatment hazard.
Pel-Ebstein/cyclical fevers >38°C without infection (B-symptom). IL-6/TNF-mediated.
Drenching night sweats requiring change of clothing — classic B-symptom.
Cachexia from chronic IL-6/TNF-mediated inflammation; >10% weight loss over 6 months defines B-symptom.
Cytokine-driven fatigue plus anemia of inflammation; affects ECOG performance status.
IL-6-driven hepatic acute phase response; CRP elevation common in advanced lymphoma without infection.
Negative acute phase reactant; hypoalbuminemia is a poor prognostic marker.
Constitutional symptoms degrade performance status; ECOG ≥2 is an IPI factor.
Marrow displacement plus chronic disease anemia → normocytic anemia.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Heavy marrow infiltration (>30%).
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Megakaryocyte displacement; thrombocytopenia worsens with treatment.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Heavy marrow infiltration.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Granulopoietic compartment displacement; baseline neutropenia complicates chemotherapy dosing.
Bone marrow biopsy confirms involvement (concordant large-cell vs discordant low-grade); upstages to stage IV.
PET/CT-defined extranodal sites; ≥2 sites is an IPI factor.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Specific high-risk extranodal sites: testis, breast, kidney/adrenal, paraspinal/epidural, multiple extranodal sites.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: These sites confer markedly elevated CNS relapse risk and inform CNS prophylaxis decisions.
MRI brain + LP cytology/flow define leptomeningeal vs parenchymal disease.
CNS relapse occurs in ~5% overall, up to 25-35% in high-risk testicular DLBCL without prophylaxis; usually within 1-2 years.
Cranial neuropathy, focal deficits, headache, encephalopathy from CNS lymphoma.
Lymphoma-related immune dysfunction stacks with chemotherapy/rituximab effects.
Encapsulated bacteria, PCP, HBV/CMV/VZV reactivation, invasive fungal infection during and post-treatment.
ANC nadir typically days 8-14 of each cycle; G-CSF shifts nadir earlier and shallower.
Febrile neutropenia in 15-25% of R-CHOP cycles without primary G-CSF prophylaxis; major cause of treatment delay.
Mild-moderate thrombocytopenia with R-CHOP; severe with DA-EPOCH-R, salvage regimens, or post-ASCT.
Neutropenic fever frequently reflects bacteremia or occult infection.
Cumulative-dose-dependent LV dysfunction; risk ~5% at 400 mg/m², ~26% at 550 mg/m². R-CHOP×6 reaches ~300 mg/m².

mechanism_edges.conditionality: HBsAg+ or HBsAg-/anti-HBc+ without prophylaxis.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Without prophylaxis, ~20-50% of HBsAg+ patients reactivate; entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis reduces risk to <5%.
Hepatitis flare with marked ALT/AST elevation; can be fulminant.
First sign of CRS; fever >38°C ASTCT grade 1 onset.
CRS grade 2-4: hypotension, requiring fluids/pressors and tocilizumab.
ICANS: confusion, aphasia, seizure, cerebral edema; ICE score-based grading.
Massive IL-6 rise during CRS; rationale for tocilizumab.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: EBV+ DLBCL subtype.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Plasma EBV-DNA often detectable in EBV+ DLBCL; correlates with tumor burden.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: EBV+ subset.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: EBV oncoproteins drive NF-kB activation and clonal proliferation.
Untreated/refractory disease progresses rapidly; ~40% of patients relapse or are refractory after first-line.
Refractory/relapsed DLBCL has historical 6-month median OS without effective salvage; CAR-T improves but not all eligible.
Hyperkalemic arrhythmia, AKI requiring dialysis, and sudden death.
Septic shock during neutropenia or post-rituximab is a leading cause of treatment-related mortality.
Late-onset heart failure contributes to non-relapse mortality, especially in older survivors.
Fulminant hepatitis post-rituximab carries high mortality without prophylaxis.
CNS relapse historically has median OS <6 months despite intensive therapy.
IPI 0-1: ~90% 5-yr OS; IPI 4-5: ~50-55% 5-yr OS in rituximab era. Composite of age, LDH, ECOG, stage, extranodal sites.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: metabolic_tumor_burden_activity is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: splenic_lesion_burden captures extranodal or organ-specific lymphoma distribution relevant before biopsy confirmation.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Most relevant when DLBCL involves spleen, mesentery, retroperitoneum, bowel, liver, or bulky abdominal nodal/extranodal sites.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Visceral or splenic DLBCL can produce early satiety before biopsy confirmation.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Most relevant when DLBCL involves spleen, mesentery, retroperitoneum, bowel, liver, or bulky abdominal nodal/extranodal sites.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Abdominal extranodal or bulky nodal DLBCL can produce pain or fullness as part of the observable clinical stack.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when the lymphoma has measurable nodal or splenic mass burden on imaging or examination.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenic involvement or splenic lymphoma burden can be followed as raw splenic size when reported.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Parent finding becomes present when the corresponding lymphoma distribution is clinically or radiographically present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenic lymphoma involvement is a parent imaging finding; size and burden are satellites/measurements.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Parent finding becomes present when the corresponding lymphoma distribution is clinically or radiographically present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Extranodal lymphoma involvement is a parent finding; organ-specific extent is a satellite.
Lymphoma cytokine activity produces recurrent or persistent fever over weeks to months.
Fever and inflammatory markers persist when the driver is lymphoma biology rather than ordinary bacterial infection.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Most prominent with pulmonary IVLBCL, mediastinal bulky disease, pleural/pericardial involvement, or severe anemia.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pulmonary, mediastinal, extranodal, or microvascular lymphoma involvement can produce breathlessness.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: More likely with airway/mediastinal compression or pulmonary infiltration.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pulmonary or mediastinal lymphoma involvement can produce cough.
Pure lymphoma fever does not produce bacterial bloodstream growth, although secondary infection can override this.
This mechanism is the imaging distribution axis itself.
Primary splenic DLBCL presents with focal or multinodular splenic lesions.
Dominant splenic involvement increases splenic lesion burden.
Bulky splenic infiltration can enlarge the spleen substantially.
Splenic parenchymal infiltration produces palpable and imaging-defined splenomegaly.
Primary splenic disease is an extranodal presentation of DLBCL.
By definition, primary splenic DLBCL can present without clinically apparent nodal disease.
Nodal activity may be absent in isolated primary splenic presentations.
Splenic capsular stretch and mass effect can cause left upper abdominal pain.
Large splenomegaly can compress the stomach and cause early satiety.
Nodal-distribution DLBCL is observed as pathologic lymph node enlargement.
Nodal-distribution DLBCL produces palpable or imaging-visible lymphadenopathy.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when nodal DLBCL involves mediastinum.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Mediastinal nodes are one possible nodal compartment in DLBCL.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when nodal DLBCL involves deep abdominal nodes.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Retroperitoneal, mesenteric, or abdominal nodal disease reflects nodal DLBCL distribution.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when nodal disease is bulky.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: High nodal burden can form bulky nodal conglomerates.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when a nodal mass is measured.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Measured nodal mass diameter is a satellite of nodal-distribution DLBCL.
DLBCL-associated IL-6/acute-phase activity and anemia can markedly raise ESR.

axes.shape_free_text: Painless rubbery node enlargement, often rapidly progressive over weeks; cervical, axillary, inguinal, or mediastinal/abdominal.
Variable; nodular or diffuse splenic infiltration on imaging.
Hepatic infiltration, less common than splenic.
Intermittent or sustained low-grade to high fever (>38°C) without infectious focus; B-symptom criterion.
Drenching nocturnal diaphoresis requiring change of clothes.
Unintentional weight loss; B-symptom defined as >10% body weight in 6 months.
Cytokine- and anemia-driven fatigue; tracks with ECOG decline.
ECOG 0-4; ≥2 is an IPI risk factor and influences treatment intensity choice.
International Prognostic Index 0-5: age >60, LDH > ULN, ECOG ≥2, stage III-IV, extranodal sites >1. NCCN-IPI uses age and LDH bands.
CNS-IPI 0-6 (IPI factors + kidney/adrenal involvement). High-risk (≥4) → ~10-12% 2-yr CNS relapse risk.
Often 1.5-5× ULN; can be markedly elevated in high-grade or bulky disease. Falls with response.
LDH/ULN ratio; >1 is IPI factor; NCCN-IPI bands at >1, >3.
Often >1000 U/mL; correlates with tumor burden and prognosis (Japanese practice).
Elevated in advanced/bulky disease; also rises with renal dysfunction.
Hypoalbuminemia from inflammation/cachexia; poor prognostic marker.
Variably elevated; high in B-symptomatic patients without infection.
Normocytic anemia of chronic disease ± marrow infiltration; deepens with chemotherapy.
Normal at baseline unless marrow infiltration; falls with chemotherapy nadirs.
Usually normal or mildly elevated; leukoerythroblastic picture if marrow infiltrated; very high in leukemic-phase HGBCL.
Lymphopenia common; ALC <1.0 is adverse prognostic factor in DLBCL.
Cyclical nadir at days 7-14 of each chemotherapy cycle; G-CSF blunts.
Elevated baseline in bulky disease; surges in TLS.
Hyperkalemia in TLS; arrhythmia risk.
Hypocalcemia in TLS due to phosphate complexation; rare hypercalcemia from PTHrP/1,25-OH-D in some lymphomas.
Hyperphosphatemia in TLS.
Rises with TLS-AKI, pre-existing CKD, or obstructive uropathy from retroperitoneal/pelvic mass.
Mild elevation with hepatic infiltration; severe rise with HBV reactivation or anti-tumor drug DILI.
Tracks with ALT in hepatic involvement or DILI/HBV reactivation.
Detectable in plasma in EBV+ DLBCL subset; falls with treatment response.
Markedly elevated during CAR-T/bispecific CRS; mildly elevated in B-symptomatic disease.
Hypotension during CRS or septic shock during neutropenia.
Hypoxia from mediastinal mass effect, pleural effusion, infection, or CRS.
Cranial neuropathy, cord compression deficit, or focal CNS lymphoma signs.
ICANS encephalopathy, CNS lymphoma, or sepsis-related delirium.
FDG-PET SUVmax usually 10-30 at diagnosis; falls below liver background on Deauville 1-3 with response.
5-point scale; D1-3 = response, D4-5 = residual/progressive disease at end-of-treatment PET.
Lugano staging derivative: nodal sites involved + bulky (>7.5-10 cm) status.
Number and burden of extranodal sites; ≥2 is IPI factor.
Bone marrow biopsy or PET-detected marrow uptake; concordant large-cell infiltration is adverse prognostic.
MRI brain + CSF flow cytometry; leptomeningeal vs parenchymal disease.
Hazard concentrated in days 0-7 of cytotoxic therapy or steroid pre-phase, particularly in bulky/high-grade disease.
Per-cycle hazard; peaks at ANC nadir (days 8-14).
Elevated throughout treatment and for months after rituximab/CAR-T due to B-cell aplasia.
Highest in first 1-2 years; concentrated in CNS-IPI high or specific high-risk extranodal sites.
~40% lifetime risk of refractory or relapsed disease; hazard highest in first 24 months.
Late-onset hazard from cumulative dose; rises beyond 300 mg/m².
Concentrated during and 6-12 months after rituximab; abrogated by entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis.
Highest with first rituximab infusion in patients with circulating CD20+ disease; cytokine release-like.
CAR-T: median onset day 2-5; bispecifics: usually first cycle day 1-3 with step-up dosing.
CAR-T: median onset day 4-10; later than CRS. Lower with liso-cel than axi-cel.
≥98% of de novo DLBCL CD20+; loss of CD20 occurs in ~10-30% at relapse post-rituximab and contraindicates further CD20-targeted therapy.
MYC + BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements (HGBCL); ~5-10% of DLBCL. Drives intensive regimen choice.
ABC (non-GCB) ~40% of DLBCL; worse prognosis with R-CHOP; Pola-R-CHP showed greater PFS benefit in non-GCB in subgroup analysis.
Baseline LVEF determines anthracycline eligibility; <50% generally contraindicates standard doxorubicin dosing → consider non-anthracycline regimens or liposomal doxorubicin.
HBsAg+, anti-HBc+, or HBV-DNA+ status mandates antiviral prophylaxis with rituximab.
Age, comorbidity, performance status, and chemosensitivity determine ASCT eligibility. Generally age <70-75 with adequate organ function.
Adequate organ function, no active CNS disease (some products allow), no uncontrolled infection, manufacturing access.
Pre-treatment diagnostic confidence in DLBCL diagnosis (excisional biopsy with CD20+ large B-cell morphology + IHC); high after biopsy.
Composite hazard: untreated aggressive disease has median OS of months; with R-CHOP, ~60% cured. Hazard concentrated in first 6 months (treatment toxicity, refractory disease) and at relapse.
Imaging-visible mediastinal lymph node enlargement or nodal packets, not the CT test itself.
Imaging-visible retroperitoneal, mesenteric, porta hepatis, para-aortic, pelvic, or other deep abdominal nodal disease.
Large confluent nodal mass or bulky nodal conglomerate by exam or imaging.
Whole-body active lymphoma burden inferred from PET avidity, multi-station mass burden, or equivalent staging imaging.
Focal or multinodular splenic lymphoma lesion burden distinct from palpable splenomegaly alone.
Early satiety or post-prandial fullness caused by splenic enlargement, abdominal mass effect, or visceral lymphoma involvement.
Abdominal or left upper quadrant pain from splenic, mesenteric, retroperitoneal, bowel, hepatic, or other abdominal lymphoma involvement.
Largest reported nodal or nodal-conglomerate diameter on CT/MRI/ultrasound or physical measurement; raw size, not a guessed severity score.
Largest splenic long-axis dimension on imaging; raw measurement when available.
Pathologic lymph node enlargement or nodal mass is present by examination or imaging. Parent finding for nodal distribution and size satellites.
Focal or multinodular splenic lesion suspicious for lymphoma is present. Parent finding for splenic lesion burden and splenic size satellites.
Extranodal mass, organ lesion, or tissue infiltration suspicious for lymphoma is present. Parent finding for organ-specific extranodal extent satellites.
History-level fever burden over days to months, distinct from a single measured body temperature.

axes.display_name: Lack of clinical response to standard antibacterial therapy
axes.shape_free_text: Persistent fever, inflammation, or organ findings despite antibacterial therapy that should have covered ordinary bacterial infection.
Patient-reported or observed breathlessness from pulmonary, cardiac, mediastinal, anemia, or systemic inflammatory involvement.
Dry or productive cough as a symptom axis; mechanism depends on pulmonary, airway, cardiac, or mediastinal involvement.
Probability that standard blood cultures grow a causative bacterium; expected to remain low in uncomplicated lymphoma fever.
Dominant splenic mass/nodular splenic infiltration with absent or minimal nodal disease at presentation.
Often elevated in inflammatory or B-symptomatic DLBCL; reflects cytokine-driven acute-phase proteins and anemia.

Nonspecific infection-like inflammatory biomarker that may rise in aggressive lymphoma, cytokine-heavy presentations, organ dysfunction, or concurrent infection; lower expected range than bacterial sepsis.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: LDH/ULN is a derived scaling of LDH; nearly perfect collinearity by construction.
Hyperuricemia precedes urate nephropathy AKI by hours to days.
Calcium phosphate precipitation tightly couples PO4 rise to Ca fall.
ANC <0.5 × 10⁹/L sharply elevates febrile neutropenia hazard.
Higher IPI predicts shorter PFS and OS.
CNS-IPI ≥4 → ~10-12% 2-yr CNS relapse vs <1% for low risk.
End-of-treatment Deauville 4-5 strongly predicts refractory/relapsed disease.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Large active lymphoma burden can raise turnover and inflammatory burden, but effect varies by subtype and bulk.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Anatomic/metabolic lymphoma burden is a driver of LDH and inflammatory marker elevation rather than a laboratory test name.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Large active lymphoma burden can raise turnover and inflammatory burden, but effect varies by subtype and bulk.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Anatomic/metabolic lymphoma burden is a driver of LDH and inflammatory marker elevation rather than a laboratory test name.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Rituximab requires CD20 expression; CD20-negative DLBCL needs alternative anti-tumor strategies.
LVEF <50% increases doxorubicin cardiotoxicity risk; consider liposomal doxorubicin or anthracycline-free regimens (R-mini-CHOP, R-GemOx).
HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ requires entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis to prevent fulminant reactivation.
R-CHOP underperforms in HGBCL with MYC + BCL2/BCL6 rearrangement; DA-EPOCH-R or Pola-R-CHP preferred.

side_effects.interpretation: Cyclical neutropenia at days 8-14 each cycle; G-CSF prophylaxis recommended for elderly/IPI-high.
Cumulative dose ~300 mg/m² across 6 cycles; late-onset HF risk.
Encapsulated organisms, PCP, herpesvirus reactivation; B-cell aplasia for 6-12 months.
First rituximab infusion, especially with high tumor burden; managed with premedication and slow titration.

treatments.context_specific_role: Standard chemoimmunotherapy backbone for newly diagnosed CD20+ DLBCL; 6 cycles standard, with possible 4 cycles in low-risk PET-negative limited stage.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: POLARIX trial showed PFS benefit largely in IPI 2-5; less benefit in IPI 0-1.
Subgroup analysis suggests greater PFS benefit in non-GCB/ABC DLBCL.
Replaces vincristine with polatuzumab (anti-CD79b ADC); maintains rituximab + anthracycline backbone.

side_effects.interpretation: Polatuzumab peripheral neuropathy, milder than vincristine in head-to-head.

treatments.context_specific_role: Alternative chemoimmunotherapy for newly diagnosed IPI 2-5 DLBCL; substitutable for R-CHOP in higher-risk or non-GCB patients.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Retrospective and prospective data favor DA-EPOCH-R over R-CHOP in HGBCL with MYC + BCL2/BCL6.
Frail/poor PS patients tolerate DA-EPOCH-R poorly; toxicity dominates.

side_effects.interpretation: More severe neutropenia than R-CHOP; mandatory G-CSF.
Higher than R-CHOP; ICU admissions more common.

treatments.context_specific_role: Intensified regimen for HGBCL/double-hit and primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma; not standard for ordinary DLBCL.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Allows curative-intent treatment in patients ≥80 or with comorbidities who cannot tolerate full-dose R-CHOP.

side_effects.interpretation: Lower neutropenia incidence than full R-CHOP.

treatments.context_specific_role: Reserved for elderly/frail patients (≥80 years or significant comorbidity); ~50% 2-yr OS in LNH-03-7B trial.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: End-of-treatment PET-positive residual disease benefits from consolidative radiation 30-40 Gy.

side_effects.interpretation: Mediastinal RT adds cardiotoxicity to anthracycline exposure.

treatments.context_specific_role: Consolidation for bulky disease (>7.5-10 cm), limited-stage disease post-R-CHOP×4, or PET-positive residual sites; definitive treatment for primary CNS, testicular, or skeletal lymphoma sanctuary sites.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Considered for CNS-IPI ≥4 or specific high-risk extranodal sites (testis, breast, kidney/adrenal).
MTX-based regimens (e.g., MATRix) for established CNS-DLBCL.
Renal impairment markedly increases MTX toxicity; aggressive hydration, urine alkalinization, and leucovorin rescue required.

side_effects.interpretation: MTX nephrotoxicity, especially with delayed clearance.

treatments.context_specific_role: Intrathecal or systemic high-dose MTX (3-3.5 g/m²) for CNS prophylaxis in high CNS-IPI or treatment of established CNS-DLBCL; debate persists about prophylactic efficacy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Generally requires age <70-75, adequate organ function, and chemosensitivity (response to salvage).
Pre-ASCT PET-negative status (Deauville 1-3) predicts much better outcomes than PET-positive.

side_effects.interpretation: Bacterial, fungal, viral infections during aplastic phase and prolonged immune reconstitution.

treatments.context_specific_role: Second-line for chemosensitive late-relapsed DLBCL (>12 months from frontline); displaced by CAR-T for early-relapsed/refractory in most settings (ZUMA-7, TRANSFORM).

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Adequate organ function, performance status, no uncontrolled infection; CD19 expression assumed in DLBCL.
Bulky disease at infusion increases CRS/ICANS severity and lowers durable response rate; bridging therapy often used.

side_effects.interpretation: Any-grade CRS in 70-95%; ≥grade 3 in 10-25% depending on product (axi-cel highest, liso-cel lowest).

treatments.context_specific_role: Frontline for primary refractory or early-relapsed (<12 months) DLBCL after ZUMA-7/TRANSFORM; also used in 3rd line+ as standard of care. Distinct products: axi-cel, liso-cel, tisa-cel.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Engages CD20 on lymphoma and CD3 on T cells; CD20-loss escape possible after rituximab pretreatment.

side_effects.interpretation: CRS during step-up dosing in cycle 1; usually grade 1-2.

treatments.context_specific_role: Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T for relapsed/refractory DLBCL after ≥2 prior lines; epcoritamab and glofitamab approved.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Studied in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL (L-MIND); chemo-free option.

side_effects.interpretation: Cumulative immunosuppression with prior anti-CD20 therapy.

treatments.context_specific_role: Transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL; alternative when CAR-T not feasible.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Approved for relapsed/refractory DLBCL not eligible for ASCT.

treatments.context_specific_role: Bridge or salvage in transplant-ineligible relapsed DLBCL.
≥3rd line relapsed/refractory DLBCL after CAR-T/bispecific failure or ineligibility.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hydrogen peroxide byproduct triggers oxidative hemolysis in G6PD deficiency.
First-line for high-risk TLS in DLBCL with bulky/high-LDH disease.

treatments.context_specific_role: Pre-emptive or therapeutic for high-risk or established TLS, especially with bulky/high-LDH DLBCL or HGBCL.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Renal dose adjustment required; rare DRESS-like hypersensitivity.

side_effects.interpretation: Allopurinol hypersensitivity, DRESS rare but serious.

treatments.context_specific_role: Standard low-to-intermediate TLS-risk prophylaxis; used with hydration. Insufficient alone for high-risk DLBCL with bulky disease/LDH ≥2× ULN.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Primary prophylaxis recommended in elderly/frail receiving R-CHOP.

treatments.context_specific_role: Primary prophylaxis for elderly/IPI-high patients on R-CHOP; secondary after febrile neutropenia or dose-limiting cytopenia; mandatory with DA-EPOCH-R.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: HBsAg+ requires prophylaxis throughout therapy and ≥12 months after; HBsAg-/anti-HBc+ requires monitoring or prophylaxis.

side_effects.interpretation: Tenofovir disoproxil renal effect; tenofovir alafenamide preferred for renal-impaired.

treatments.context_specific_role: Mandatory for HBsAg+ patients on rituximab-containing therapy; consider for anti-HBc+ patients.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: ALC <0.5 × 10⁹/L during steroid + rituximab use elevates PCP risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: PCP prophylaxis during R-CHOP and beyond; commonly continued through R-CHOP and 3-6 months post.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: First-line for grade ≥2 CAR-T/bispecific CRS.

side_effects.interpretation: Masks CRP/fever; reactivation of latent infections.

treatments.context_specific_role: Acute treatment of CAR-T/bispecific CRS; less effective for ICANS, where corticosteroids are first-line.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Corticosteroids first-line for ICANS grade ≥2; methylprednisolone pulse for grade 3-4.

treatments.context_specific_role: Acute treatment of CAR-T/bispecific ICANS; theoretical concern about CAR-T persistence is outweighed by safety in grade ≥2 ICANS.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Maintain urine output >100 mL/m²/hr; alkalinization no longer routinely recommended due to calcium phosphate precipitation risk.

side_effects.interpretation: Alkalinization can precipitate calcium phosphate; dilutional hypocalcemia possible.

treatments.context_specific_role: Backbone of TLS prevention; started 24-48h before cytoreductive therapy.

age_above_60.trajectory_modulation: Higher IPI risk band; greater treatment toxicity and lower fitness for intensive regimens.

age_above_80.trajectory_modulation: Often R-mini-CHOP; cure rates lower; treatment-related mortality higher.

hiv_positive_uncontrolled.trajectory_modulation: AIDS-defining illness; concurrent ART required; outcomes approach HIV-negative when CD4 preserved.

solid_organ_transplant_recipient.trajectory_modulation: Often EBV-driven post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) presenting as DLBCL morphology; reduction of immunosuppression and rituximab are first steps.

ebv_positive_dlbcl_subtype.trajectory_modulation: Worse outcomes with R-CHOP; older age skew.

rheumatoid_arthritis_or_sjogren_or_sle.trajectory_modulation: Chronic immune stimulation predisposes; methotrexate-associated lymphoproliferative disorder may regress on drug withdrawal.

hcv_chronic_infection.trajectory_modulation: Some marginal-zone-derived DLBCL cases regress with antiviral therapy.

male.trajectory_modulation: Slight male predominance; testicular DLBCL is a unique sanctuary site.

supportive_care: Pre-treatment excisional biopsy (preferred over core/FNA) for histopathology, IHC (CD20, CD3, CD5, CD10, BCL2, BCL6, MUM1, MYC, Ki-67, EBER-ISH), and FISH for MYC/BCL2/BCL6 rearrangements; cell-of-origin classification (Hans algorithm or GEP).
Staging with whole-body PET-CT (Lugano), bone marrow biopsy if PET ambiguous, MRI brain + LP for CNS-IPI high or high-risk extranodal sites.
Baseline echocardiogram or MUGA to confirm LVEF ≥50% before anthracycline.
Pre-treatment HBV serology (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs, HBV-DNA), HCV serology, HIV testing; pregnancy testing in women of childbearing potential.
Tumor lysis risk stratification (Cairo-Bishop): aggressive hydration, allopurinol for low-intermediate risk, rasburicase for high-risk (bulky/high-LDH) or HGBCL.
Primary G-CSF prophylaxis for elderly (≥65) or IPI-high patients on R-CHOP; mandatory for DA-EPOCH-R.
PCP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) during chemoimmunotherapy and 3-6 months post; consider for prolonged steroid use.
HBV antiviral prophylaxis (entecavir/tenofovir) for HBsAg+ patients during therapy and ≥12 months post; surveillance HBV-DNA for HBsAg-/anti-HBc+.
Antiviral prophylaxis (acyclovir/valacyclovir) for VZV/HSV reactivation, especially during CAR-T/bispecifics.
Antifungal prophylaxis (e.g., posaconazole) selectively in prolonged neutropenia or post-allo-SCT.
Vaccinations: inactivated influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19 (response may be blunted); avoid live vaccines during and 6-12 months post-rituximab.
Fertility preservation counseling (sperm banking, ovarian tissue cryopreservation) before cyclophosphamide-containing therapy in patients of reproductive age.
Cardiac surveillance during and after anthracycline (echocardiogram, BNP, troponin); consider dexrazoxane for high cumulative-dose patients.
Vincristine peripheral neuropathy monitoring with possible dose reduction or omission.
Mucositis and infection surveillance during nadirs; thresholds for empiric antibiotic initiation in febrile neutropenia.
Psychosocial support, patient/family education on B-symptoms vs infection, and symptom-directed palliative care for refractory disease.
Long-term survivorship: secondary malignancy surveillance (especially MDS/AML after alkylators), cardiovascular risk modification, fatigue and cognitive symptom management.
CAR-T-specific: caregiver requirement, 30-day proximity to treatment center, IgG monitoring with IVIG replacement if recurrent infection, prolonged cytopenia management.
End-of-treatment PET-CT with Deauville scoring for response assessment; surveillance imaging individualized as routine surveillance has limited survival benefit in CR patients.
